title: Deconstructing Demand
summary:
Deconstructing Demand
Although crude oil prices have been over $100 per barrel for several months, worldwide demand has yet to be materially affected. Some recent evidence indicates that demand in the United States may now be on the decline; in addition, it seems that United States consumption might be losing its title as the barometer of worldwide sentiment. The International Energy Agency pegged global oil demand for the second quarter of 2008 at just over 86 million barrels per day, marking a decline of less than one percent from the previous quarter.

children.title: North America
children.summary: OECD Europe China Non-OECD Asia Latin America Middle East Africa The United States long-standing status as the single largest oil consumer creates a tendency to focus only on the US market. In fact, the United States is becoming a smaller portion of the total demand picture.

children.title: Total Demand
children.summary: % of Total The United States' share of global demand is expected to decline about 2 percentage points between 2006 and 2009.

children.title: Looking East
children.summary: The real growth story for demand continues to be East of Suez, primarily in China, India and other emerging economies. The two major factors facilitating demand growth in these countries are industrialization and the roles of government in commodity markets.
